correctness.rationale: The full continuum derivation integrates the SIR equations to \(H=B+T(1-e^{-H})\) with \(B>0\). The unique positive root satisfies \(Te^{-H}=(H-B)/(e^H-1)<1\), even at/below \(T=1\), so H is strictly increasing in T. The fixed-budget optimum is exactly the weighted threshold exchange for maximizing integral r v, and a separate strictly improving allocation proves budget saturation at all \(K\). Rearrangement gives the exact continuum frontier and positive derivative at quantile continuity points. Endpoints \(K=0\) and \(K=S\), cut-off ties and arbitrary positive initial seeds are included. The standalone checker verifies 125 rational-grid cases and two direct ODE integrations but is not used as an infinite proof. Scientific limitations: identical susceptibility and perfect instantaneous vaccine; dynamic supremum consequence depends on pre-existing source Theorem 3.

originality.rationale: A recent primary source (arXiv:2605.18256v1, Theorem 4) establishes the threshold allocation only under its displayed small-budget bound and expressly conjectures that this bound can be removed (Remark 1.4). The present theorem does so for every admissible budget and derives the exact full survivor frontier including the subcritical range. Source Theorem 3 all-time supremum equivalence, the priority order itself, and tied-level-set allowance are acknowledged prior, not claimed new. Highly relevant older 2016 separable-mixing literature optimizes minimum critical supply, not the full fixed-budget positive-seed epidemic size. Residual risk: an unindexed stronger special-case theorem might imply this result.
residual_risks: An older general vaccine-allocation theorem specialized to a rank-one common-hazard kernel may already imply fixed-budget all-range optimality; none found in the searches and inspected highly relevant full texts.
The absence of a semantic database match does not establish independent novelty.
Earlier critical-reproduction-number knapsack optimizers share the priority ordering, so only the unrestricted-budget survivor optimality and full frontier are asserted as new.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper identifies removal of the small-supply hypothesis as a meaningful open calculation (Remark 1.4). The present exact all-K optimization resolves the entire missing parameter range, not a cosmetic bound, and gives a constructive all-supply policy and quantitative dose-response curve. Its proof handles the threshold crossing that invalidated the previous monotonicity shortcut and treats all end budgets and tied priority classes; a high-budget two-class example \(K=1.5\) exceeds the published \(K<1.25\) condition. General clinical relevance is not asserted beyond a stylized common-susceptibility SIR model.
